about: The access that Meternaut needs outside its own resource group. Meternaut holds no write right: every grant below only reads, and a change to Azure is made with the token of the person who approved it, so that Azure checks that person's own rights (docs/proposals/03-access-and-onboarding.md). The deployment workflow's identity holds no right there and must not get one (AGENTS.md rule 18), so a person who may assign roles at each place grants it. Each line of grants is one role of one identity at one place. An identity is what a function app runs as, and the principals that hold its grants are listed as its holders: the app's own system-assigned identity, found on the app with the option that siteOption names. While an app is moved between kinds of identity, both kinds are holders (a user-assigned one has a name), so that the app is never without access. The list retired records what an earlier version granted and must now be removed: either a custom role that is no longer wanted at all (every assignment of it, then the role), or, with replacedBy, a grant of an identity that an app no longer runs as (only that identity's own assignment: the role stays, because the grant that replaces it needs it), or, with roleStays, a grant of a built-in role that nothing needs any more (only the own assignment of the identities that the item names, never anybody else's: the role is built in and stays). tools/access-requirements.py reads this file: it checks what is granted, grants what is missing only with --apply, and with retire removes what is retired, again only with --apply. On 2026-11-07 the owner ordered the undo of what Meternaut added to his API Management instance: the cases app reads no key any more, so the custom role that read one (W7) and its grant are retired, and retire removes every assignment of that role at the instance's resource group and below it, then the role. The deployment identity's own custom role in that group (W8) is retired the same way, because no Hub action uses it since the actions that made objects on the instance were removed. The same day the owner ordered the usage recording removed, because nothing fed it any more: the usage app read the old gateway's telemetry, so its two reads (Monitoring Reader on the gateway's Application Insights, and a custom role on the central workspace that read one table) are retired as W9 and W10, and the Hub action retire-old deletes the usage app. Run retire for W9 before that action, while the usage app and its identity still exist, because an assignment of a deleted identity cannot be traced to it. On 2026-11-07 the owner ordered that the Watch watch the entire estate: the cases app reads every subscription that its identity can read, so R1 and R2 are given once, by a person and outside the template, at the tenant root management group (or at each subscription, to watch only those); this file and the template give nothing there. docs/proposals/03-access-and-onboarding.md shows the two tables that the tool prints, and a test keeps them the same. On 2026-11-08 the capability profile (cases/capability.py) added four reads: the price sheet of one subscription, which R2 covers, and the lists of billing accounts, reservation orders and savings plan orders, which no Azure role at a subscription or a management group gives (they are at the tenant or at a billing scope), so they are listed apart under tenantReads, as T1 to T3, for a person to give; this tool neither checks nor gives them, and the app says 'not visible with this access' until they are given.

places.estate: The estate that the Watch reads: the tenant root management group (the Watch then reads every subscription that its identity can read: the app setting SCOPE_ALL_SUBSCRIPTIONS), or each subscription one by one (the app setting SCOPE_SUBSCRIPTIONS, which is also the fallback)
places.gatewayInsights: The old gateway's Application Insights component
places.gatewayGroup: The resource group of the owner's API Management instance, and everything below it
places.centralWorkspace: The central workspace that the component writes to, and the resource group that holds it
places.projectGroup: The project's own resource group, where Meternaut plants waste of its own

grants.why: Reads the list of the subscriptions that the identity can read (the Watch reads every one of them), their resources, tags and management locks, Azure Advisor's cost recommendations, the platform metrics that Azure Monitor keeps for a resource and the pricing settings of the Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans: the detectors, the guards and the read-only tools of the investigator. The tools also read, from the Resource Manager, the settings and the tables of a workspace for logs, its saved searches and its Microsoft Sentinel rules, the workbooks of a subscription, the diagnostic settings of a resource, the deployments of an AI services account and the Activity Log (who made or last changed a resource, for the human brief only), and, from the workspace's query API, the volume of the data that a workspace takes in, with queries of fixed text that code made and that name no text from the estate. The role's rights (`*/read`) already include reading the data of a workspace; Meternaut asks only for volumes, counts and the names of the platform's own tables, shows no record, and is held to that by its tests, and a workspace that is set to refuse the read (a protected table, or the access mode that needs a data action) answers 'not visible with this access'. It also reads, in the project's own resource group, the resource that a change is made on (a managed disk, a public IP address, a virtual machine with the sizes that it can take and its instance view, a snapshot, a network interface, a NAT gateway, a load balancer or a private endpoint) and the regional quota of vCPUs, when a plan is written and when the timer checks what a change did. A person gives it at the tenant root management group or each subscription: at the group the Watch reads the entire estate, at a subscription only that one. The role reads and changes nothing

Reads the cost lines of every resource for the last 30 days, and the cost of one resource or one type by day for up to 90 days, actual or amortized, so that every figure is Cost Management's and never a model's. It also reads how the cost of the last 30 days was paid for (amortized, by pricing model and kind of charge) and the platform's own purchase recommendations for savings plans (Microsoft.CostManagement) and for reservations (Microsoft.Consumption), which this role holds as `*/read` of those two providers. It also reads one line of the price sheet of the first subscription of a run (Microsoft.Consumption), only to learn whether the price sheet is readable at all: an agreement may still refuse it, and then the capability profile says 'not visible with this access'. The utilization of a reservation or a savings plan is read at a billing scope or at the reservation itself, which this role does not give: the tools do not read it. A person gives it at the tenant root management group or each subscription, with R1; without it a subscription is still read, and the History says that its cost lines could not be read

tenantReads.read: The billing accounts that the identity has access to, with the agreement type that each reports
roles: Microsoft Customer Agreement: a billing role, Billing account reader (or Billing profile reader, for one billing profile).
Enterprise Agreement: the billing role Enterprise administrator (read-only).
The role is given in the Billing area of the portal, by a billing administrator: it is not an Azure role, so no Azure role at a subscription or a management group gives it.
tenantReads.why: The capability profile (cases/capability.py) tells which agreement the estate is under, and so what the decision brief can say about commitments. Until a person gives the role, the list is empty or refused, and the profile says 'not visible with this access': never that there is no agreement

tenantReads.read: The reservation orders that the identity has access to in the tenant
roles: Azure role: Reservations Reader, assigned at the tenant scope /providers/Microsoft.Capacity (it needs a person with User Access Administrator rights there: Learn, 'Grant RBAC access to reservations by using PowerShell').
Or a billing role: Microsoft Customer Agreement, billing profile Reader or higher; Enterprise Agreement, Enterprise administrator (read-only) or higher; Microsoft Partner Agreement, not supported.
tenantReads.why: The capability profile tells whether the existing reservations can be seen, so that no tool and no brief says that the estate has none when the identity only cannot see them. The read lists the orders and nothing of what they cover

tenantReads.read: The savings plan orders that the identity has access to
roles: Azure role: Savings plan reader, assigned at the tenant scope /providers/Microsoft.BillingBenefits (Learn, 'Permissions to view and manage savings plans').
Or a billing role: Microsoft Customer Agreement, billing profile reader or above; Enterprise Agreement, enterprise administrator (read only) or above; Microsoft Partner Agreement, not supported.
tenantReads.why: The same for savings plans: whether the existing ones can be seen. The read lists the orders and nothing of what they cover

retired.why: The writer of an earlier version: a custom role that read and deleted a managed disk and a public IP address in this group, held by this identity. Meternaut holds no write right now: a change is made with the token of the person who approved it, and Azure checks that person's own rights. The role's assignments and the role are removed with retire; the identity is removed by the deployment workflow or by the owner
Held by the user-assigned identity that the cases app ran as before its own system-assigned identity took over (R1). Only that identity's assignment is removed, and the role stays: R1 needs it
Held by the user-assigned identity that the cases app ran as before its own system-assigned identity took over (R2). Only that identity's assignment is removed, and the role stays: R2 needs it

A custom role of an earlier version that read one key of one subscription of the owner's API Management instance (and nothing else), so that the cases app could call the models through that instance. It was held by the cases app's own system-assigned identity and, before that, by this user-assigned identity. The owner ordered the undo of what Meternaut added to that instance on 2026-11-07, and the app reads no key any more: it calls the models of its own Foundry project with its own identity. Every assignment of the role at the instance's resource group and below it is removed, whoever holds it, and then the role itself

A custom role of the first environment that the deployment workflow's identity held in the resource group of the owner's API Management instance, so that the Hub could add Citadel's objects to the instance, attach an identity to it and make the access product of the first cases on it. No Hub action uses it since 2026-11-07: the owner ordered the undo of what Meternaut added to that instance, and the actions that made those objects were removed. Every assignment of the role at the instance's resource group and below it is removed, whoever holds it, and then the role itself. The identity stays: it deploys the project's own resource group, and it lives in the bootstrap group, so it is not looked up

The usage app's read of the old gateway's Application Insights component, where the gateway recorded the token metrics of every call, so that the copy jobs of the usage recording could copy them. The owner ordered the usage recording removed on 2026-11-07, because nothing fed it any more: the app is deleted by the Hub action retire-old. The role is built in and stays, because other people hold it. Only the own assignments of the two identities that the usage app ran as are removed: its system-assigned identity, found by reading the app named by --usage-site, and the user-assigned identity id-meternaut-usage that it ran as before. Run this before the Hub action retire-old, while the app and the identity still exist: an assignment of a deleted identity cannot be traced to it

A custom role of the usage recording that read one table (AppMetrics, the metrics of workspace-based Application Insights) of the central workspace, so that its copy jobs could read the gateway's token metrics, and nothing else. It was defined in the resource group of that workspace and held by the usage app's own system-assigned identity and, before that, by the user-assigned identity id-meternaut-usage. Nothing reads those metrics any more (the owner ordered the usage recording removed on 2026-11-07). Every assignment of the role at the workspace's resource group and below it is removed, whoever holds it, and then the role itself
